page: Amazon Web Services u-6tb1.112xlarge is a memory-optimized instance designed for large-scale in-memory workloads. It features 448 vCPUs and 224 physical cores powered by Intel Xeon 8176M processors operating at 2.1 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is equipped with 6144.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing approximately 13.71 GB of RAM per core. It utilizes the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

In benchmark testing, the u-6tb1.112xlarge demonstrates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, as evidenced by its top 10% rankings in stress-ng multi-core, PassMark CPU, and PassMark CPU extended instructions tests. Memory bandwidth is also highly competitive, achieving top-tier results in both cached small-block and uncached large-block read/write operations. However, single-core performance is more modest, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the average and weak categories, respectively. Additionally, PassMark memory score and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression benchmarks register in the bottom 25%, indicating potential latency or throughput bottlenecks under specific memory-access patterns.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance represents a specialized, high-density hardware class where the premium is justified by the massive memory footprint rather than raw single-threaded speed. It is best suited for large in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning systems, and massive data-processing pipelines that require up to 6 TB of RAM. It is not recommended for workloads requiring local NVMe storage, high-speed single-threaded execution, or GPU acceleration.
